class: A database CHECK written as JSON-path filters over a free JSONB document refuses only the shapes its author listed: PostgreSQL's default lax mode unwraps an array wherever the path expects a scalar, so a value wrapped in an array (or an empty array) satisfies every per-value test, and a position whose value is only type-checked accepts any text of that type. A shape CHECK built this way is a list of refused forms, not a closed description of the allowed document.
mechanism: W-061 round 2 enforced the strategy definition's closed key shape with jsonpath CHECKs in default (lax) mode and per-leg type tests only; as ofo_app, inserts with preferences {"objective":["income"]}, risk_limits {"max_loss":["9000"]}, rules_ref ["abc"], legs [[leg]], legs [], and leg values strike "LTP 22950.35", action "LTP is 22950.35 buy now", quantity 22950.35 were all accepted, so a live price could be stored inside a strategy (REQ-038 AC-5).

first_seen.evidence: Tier A review attack script as ofo_app (each ACCEPTED, rolled back); reproduced by the orchestrator with a throwaway pytest reusing test_strategy_closed_shape.py fixtures on the real ofo_test database: 6 of 6 cases 'DID NOT RAISE' (pref-array, risk-array, rules-ref-array, leg-strike-sentence, leg-action-sentence, leg-quantity-fraction); the branch's own 27 closed-shape tests were green

fix: Open for round 3 (issue #165): an independent review compares strict-mode jsonpath with a per-position value check, one positive whitelist validation function, and typed relational columns; the round-3 test list includes a positive enumeration (every JSON type other than the allowed one, at every position of the closed shape, is refused).

detection.note: The round-3 positive enumeration test is the planned detection; until it merges, W-061 does not merge.
